newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Nervous Euro-bourses fall ahead of U.S. data.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Nervous Euro-bourses fall ahead of U.S. data.

text.p: Europe's share market rally took a breather on Thursday as nervous investors turned their attention to key U.S. payrolls figures due out on Friday.
London popped up to a fresh trading high before going into retreat along with the Paris bourse.
With German markets closed for the country's reunification holiday, foreign exchange markets were relatively quiet.
Nervousness ahead of Friday's U.S. September jobs numbers was also seen keeping a lid on both equity and dollar gains.
But French and British government bonds, or gilts, jumped in early trading following a U.S. bond rally overnight, although traders said the U.S. data could prompt profit-taking.
"We were looking for gilts to rally over the past week, and they have done. But this morning things have really gone berserk," said David Coleman, chief economist at CIBC Wood Grundy in London.
In contrast, gold eased again and aluminium slumped to a 2-1/4 year low on the London Metal Exchange, with higher supplies meeting declining demand in Europe.
The dollar held steady in early European trade, holding above 1.53 marks but still off an overnight high of 112 yen.
"The dollar is beginning to look a bit heavy and the 112 yen level is a big stumbling block," said a Swiss bank dealer.
Talk of capital flowing out of Japan kept the yen depressed but analysts were cautious over whether these flows were actually materialising.

"The funding of carry trades by speculative players is perhaps a more convincing rationalisation of continued yen weakness," said Paul Meggyesi, senior currency economist at Deutsche Morgan Grenfell in London.
By 0900 GMT the dollar was quoted around 111.50 yen and 1.5321 marks versus Wednesday's late European levels of 111.75 and 1.5277.
Wall Street's fresh record overnight was not enough to keep European equity markets up at Wednesday's peaks.

London's blue chip FTSE 100 index, which cleared the 4,000 hurdle for the first time on Wednesday, edged up to a fresh trading peak of 4,024.3 in early trade before turning down. By 0900 GMT the index was showing a loss of nearly nine points.

"The (U.S. jobs) numbers are pretty crucial and we usually live in fear of them for about a week before they're out. We may see some short-term profit-taking at some stage but I don't think it will take too much froth off the market," said one trader.

Among individual stocks, shares in P&O jumped 28-1/2p to a their highest level in more than a year at 653-1/2p after news that it would merge its short-sea ferry business on the English Channel with those of Swedish rival Stena Line.
In Paris, French shares shaded back opening gains as the market consolidated Wednesday's 0.88 percent rise and the October CAC future slipped.
Food group Bongrain fell 10.87 percent after announcing first half-profit dropped 21 percent. The shares were suspended limit-down at the opening of trade.
CURRENCIES AT 0900 GMT
The dollar traded around 111.50 yen and 1.5321 marks versus Wednesday's late European levels of 111.75 and 1.5277.
STOCK MARKETS AT 0900 GMT
London - The Financial Times-Stock Exchange index of 100 leading shares was down 8.7 points at 4,006.4.
Paris - The CAC-40 share index was down 5.82 points at 2,136.02.
Frankfurt - The market was closed for a holiday. The 30-share DAX index closed on Wednesday at 2,676.5.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold was fixed at $379.50 an ounce in the morning, versus $380.35 previously, in very quiet trading. Silver was little changed at 492 cents.
